title: They weren’t protecting Jesus.
paragraphs: They thought they were doing the right thing.

Because in Gospel of Mark 10, the disciples didn’t shout “No!” out of hatred… they resisted out of misplaced priority. Children were “too small,” too insignificant, too unimportant for the Master’s time.
Let that settle in your bones.
The same Jesus who calmed storms burned with emotion when people were being kept away from Him. And He said, “Let the little children come to me; do not hinder them…” (Mark 10:14).
So here’s the question that cuts deeper than we want:
What if you’re not far from Jesus… but you’re still standing in the way?
What if your life looks “close” to Him—but your heart has learned how to filter who deserves Him?
Sometimes the greatest resistance to grace doesn’t come from the world.
It comes from people who already know His name.
With that quiet thought: “They’ll understand later… this isn’t for them yet.”
Because this isn’t just about how we treat others.
This is about how we treat our own soul.
But how many times have you held yourself back?
Because of the quiet voice that whispers, “You’re not clean enough yet.”
Here’s the hidden struggle no one posts about:
You believe Jesus forgives others faster than He forgives you.
You carry guilt Jesus already nailed to the cross.
“There is therefore now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus” (Romans 8:1).
So why are you still standing outside what He already opened?
Why are you resisting the very grace you preach?
Some of us are discipling others into freedom… while secretly living in chains.
That’s the quiet hypocrisy we don’t name.
Because it looks holy on the outside.
You’re tired of trying to earn what was already given.
And that’s where the scene shifts.
Because Mark 10 doesn’t end with rejection.
It ends with Jesus touching them.
He didn’t just allow the children.
Because the Kingdom of God is not entered by the strong.
It is received by the surrendered.
Jesus said whoever does not receive the Kingdom like a child shall not enter it (Mark 10:15).
The only thing blocking you from Jesus… might be the version of yourself trying to be worthy of Him.
Let that break something in you.
“Come, and I will make you new.”
“All have sinned and fall short of the glory of God” (Romans 3:23).
But the story doesn’t end there.
Because Jesus stepped into our mess.
And rose again—so that whoever believes in Him would not perish but have eternal life (John 3:16).
But it requires something we resist:
You cannot enter the Kingdom while protecting your pride.
but it will cost you your illusion of self-sufficiency.
Are you coming to Jesus like a child…
or are you standing at a distance, trying to look strong?
Because He doesn’t bless the qualified.
Come with your secret struggle you’ve never said out loud.
And receive what you’ve been resisting.
Not noise. Not pressure. Just truth that feeds your soul.
We’re going deeper into the kind of faith that looks weak… but moves heaven.
